subject: Sampling discrete missing values when using custom distributions

messages.author: 63cc02caac0434cf
messages.subject: Sampling discrete missing values when using custom distributions
parts:
Hello,

In an autoregressive Poisson model with missing values, Nimble will assign slice samplers to the missing values and only sample discrete values. I will attach a simple reproducible example "test_missing_poisson.R" to illustrate what I mean.

However, in an autoregressive count model using a custom discrete distribution (like a negative binomial hurdle in the following example) with missing values, Nimble will assign RW samplers to the missing values. Even after assigning slice samplers to the missing values, Nimble still samples continuous values. For some reason, the slice sampler does not recognize the discreteness of the missing values. I will attach a simple reproducible example "test_missing_nbhurdle.R" to illustrate what I mean.

Please let me know how to get Nimble to treat the custom discrete distribution like the Poisson when sampling missing values.

Thank you!

messages.author: 7878556d408ec9ec
messages.subject: Re: Sampling discrete missing values when using custom distributions
parts:
Hi,

I think this is because your neg-bin hurdle distribution is a user-defined distribution (but you did not specify the type of the distribution) while Poisson is provided by nimble (and it knows Poisson is discrete). For a user-defined distribution, you will need to let nimble know if it is continuous or discrete. By default, nimble assumes it is continuous. You specify your distribution to be discrete by using the registerDistributions function: 

registerDistributions(list(
  dhurdleNegBinMarg = list(
    BUGSdist = "dhurdleNegBinMarg(p, lambda, r)",
    types = c('value = double(0)', 'p = double(0)', 'lambda = double(0)', 'r = double(0)'),
    discrete = TRUE
  )
))

Hope it helps.

Best wishes,
Wei

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Sampling discrete missing values when using custom distributions
parts:
Hi Dirk,
I'm glad you're on track to get this working. In nimble models, all values are implemented as doubles, even if they will only ever be integers. (Indeed, this is a reason why one needs to indicate via registerDistributions if the values really will be integers (discrete).) Hence, it works to keep the value as double(0) and we normally recommend always using doubles since that's what they will be in the implementation. However, since it is a scalar, in this case integer(0) should I think also work. (In other words, it shouldn't matter.)
Perry
